articles.title: Danny DeVito-Produced SXSW Heist Comedy ‘Drag’ Scores Wave of International Sales Out of AFM (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: “Drag,” the SXSW heist comedy starring Lizzy Caplan and John Stamos and produced by Danny DeVito, has secured a run of international deals following the American Film Market. U.K.
body: In North America, Briarcliff Entertainment holds rights and will open the film in theaters on Jan. 29, 2027.

From filmmakers Greg Yagolnitzer and Raviv Ullman, “Drag” centers on two sisters who don’t get along and who set out to burgle a remote house in upstate New York. The job goes wrong fast. One sister puts her back out and can’t move from the upper floor, and the pair must find a way out before the owner gets home. Lucy DeVito and Christine Ko round out the cast.

Danny, Lucy and Jake DeVito produced through Jersey Films 2nd Avenue, the production company they founded, and the film is the company’s first independent feature. The outfit’s earlier credits include FXX animated series “Little Demon” and Amazon sports docuseries “Game 7.” Its new film arm is set up to back original filmmakers and stories that cross genre lines.
After its premiere at SXSW in 2026, “Drag” went on to play festivals including BiFan, Beyond Fest, Fantasia and Sitges.

articles.title: Hollywood Gets Roasted in Satirical Picture Book ‘We Make a Movie’: ‘I Loved Your Script … Now Change Everything’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: “I loved your script. It is perfect. Now change everything.” While probably far from a joke for many screenwriters who have had similar conversations, this particular line is taken from upcoming satirical picture book “We Make a Movie.” Designed to look like a children’s book from the 1960s…
body: “The script says Paris by dawn. The tax break says Eastern Europe,” reads another page likely to make more than a few producers nod knowingly. “‘I loved your film,’ says the sales agent. He has not seen it,” adds another.

“Every page comes from something true,” said Follows, who has published more than 600 data-led studies of the industry and is regularly cited in the press. “Anyone in the business will recognize it, and the people it’s about will laugh along without realizing it’s them.”

Due out next month, “We Make a Movie” has already become something of a hit in the film industry. Pre-orders for the first edition (available to order at www.wemakeamovie.com ) are on course to sell out, with a second run being planned.
“‘We Make a Movie’ is the book of the year — it explains the film industry in a nutshell and in the most entertaining and funny way ever,” said Uwe Boll. “I loved it! A lot of truth to it.”

articles.title: AI Horror Short ‘Sikkal’ Wins WIF India x Google Flow Filmathon as Director Promita Banerjee Aims to Make ‘Films With Humans’
articles.summary: A horror short rooted in the toll of sickle cell disease on India’s tribal communities has won the inaugural WIF India x Google Flow Filmathon. Promita Banerjee’s “Sikkal,” made with Google’s AI creative workspace Google Flow, took the INR1.2 million ($12,500) first prize.
body: Women in Film India (WIF India) ran the Filmathon with Google Flow to open up AI filmmaking tools to emerging storytellers around the country. The call drew more than 850 registrations, and a seven-member jury that included directors Shakun Batra and Pan Nalin and Cannes Next head Sten Saluveer narrowed the field to five. The finalists were showcased at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Aamir Khan Productions CEO Aparna Purohit delivered a keynote at the event.

Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant attended the ceremony, where WIF India founder and CEO Guneet Monga Kapoor and filmmaker Ashutosh Gowariker joined the presenters on stage. Srishti Chaudhary’s “Nazar” and Aswathi Naduthodi’s “Bombay Mumbai – Vada Pav” were recognized as finalists.

articles.title: Mike Newell Recalls Being Shot at in Colombia While Filming ‘Love in the Time of Cholera’ With Giovanna Mezzogiorno: ‘She Was Like, “F— All This!”’
articles.summary: This year’s Torino Film Festival opened with a valentine to British artists, as directors Stephen Frears and Mike Newell collected lifetime achievement awards ahead of a screening of “November 1963,” the latest from Palme d’Or winner Roland Joffé.
body: So when Newell took the stage to accept his Stella della Mole trophy, he began by paying tribute to a friendship that took root at the University of Cambridge in the early 1960s.
“It’s lovely to be in the same hall as my old friend Stephen Frears, whom I have known since I was 18 years old,” he said to booming applause. “We go a ways back.”

Accepting his award from Italian actress Giovanna Mezzogiorno, Newell also recalled the less-than-ideal conditions surrounding their 2007 collaboration, “Love in the Time of Cholera,” which was shot in Colombia, with Javier Bardem, Liev Schreiber and Benjamin Bratt also in the cast.
Frears, meanwhile, drew plenty of laughs by thumbing post-Brexit wounds. “I’m English,” he reminded the Turin crowd. “Do you remember England? Once we were European!”

articles.title: Veteran Nigerian Nollywood actor Pete Edochie dies aged 79
articles.summary: Odochie rose to prominence in 1987 after starring in a television adaptation of Chinua Achebe's acclaimed novel Things Fall Apart.
body: Veteran Nigerian actor Pete Edochie, one of Africa's most celebrated film stars, has died at the age of 79, his family has announced.

Known for his deep voice, commanding screen presence and memorable use of African proverbs, Edochie became a household name across Africa, often portraying powerful traditional rulers, wealthy businessmen and family patriarchs.
In a statement, his family said Edochie died in the early hours of Wednesday in the south-eastern Nigerian city of Enugu following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer.
Tributes are pouring in from fans and fellow actors, remembering him as a Nollywood legend who helped shape Nigeria's film industry.

articles.title: Hundreds complain about I'm A Celebrity after Mariella Frostrup called AJ Odudu 'aggressive'
articles.summary: More than 800 viewers complain to regulator Ofcom after a row between AJ Odudu and Mariella Frostrup.
body: More than 800 people have complained to the media regulator about an episode of ITV reality show I'm A Celebrity... Get Me Out of Here! in which Mariella Frostrup accused her campmate AJ Odudu of being "aggressive".
Ofcom said 887 people had filed complaints about Sunday's episode in relation to "alleged bullying behaviour" by Frostrup towards Odudu.
An Ofcom spokesperson told BBC News: "We are assessing the complaints against our rules, but are yet to decide whether or not to investigate."

The pair were seen clearing the air on Tuesday, with broadcaster Frostrup saying she was "sorry for calling you aggressive" and Odudu telling her it is "a strong word to use in casual scenarios, particularly towards black women".

articles.title: ‘The Body’ Star Kristina Bogic Just Wanted to Take Care of Anya: “A Lot of Young Women Can Relate”
articles.summary: The 19-year-old star of Netflix's latest hit breaks down how she came to love her dance team captain character: "Anya always wants to try and do the right thing."
body: The Body team searched far and wide to find their leading lady, Anya. Kristina Bogic, the 19-year-old who landed the role, knew there were plenty of others trying for the part. “A lot of my friends had auditioned for Anya,” she tells The Hollywood Reporter.

Bogic did four chemistry reads with Sara Boustany, who plays Anya’s best friend and secret romantic interest Elise in the series. The actress had “a bunch” of callbacks — she just kept getting more scripts. “I remember thinking even if I wasn’t in this show, I would just be so excited to watch it,” she says.

The raunchy psychological thriller has become an online favorite. Bogic felt protective over the character from moment one. “I can’t believe I get to play Anya,” the actress says. “I really just wanted to take care of her the whole time.”

Anya’s the captain of her Catholic high school’s dance team. In addition to mass hysteria incidents, the teen’s also dealing with complicated feelings for her best friend. Bogic wanted to keep the character tucked safely under her wing.

articles.title: AI-generated voice of late commentator John Motson added to EA Sports FC video game
articles.summary: The AI-generated Motson will appear in the game on 26 November, with the consent of his son and wife.
body: Football game EA Sports FC will feature the digitally recreated voice of the late commentator John Motson, Electronic Arts has exclusively told the BBC.
Motson, who died in 2023, was the main commentator for BBC Sport for decades - and performed the same role for the video game series during the 90s and 00s.
It is the first time the hit series, formerly known as Fifa, has featured a deceased commentator.
With the permission of his widow and his son, Motson's voice has been synthesised using a combination of old recording sessions and generative AI. It will become available in FC 27 on 26 November.

articles.title: The Lord Of The Rings: The Rings Of Power Season 3's Shocking Death Leaves Its Biggest Question Unanswered
articles.summary: Another key character kicks the bucket in the Rings of Power Season 3 finale, leaving a major mystery involving the Witch-king to be resolved down the line.
body: In the land of Mordor, where the spoilers lie. This article covers major plot details from the Season 3 finale of "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power."
Either way, RIP Pallando, the most gloriously bearded wizard in all of Middle-earth (and with an attitude to match).

Well, it's more complicated than that. Theo's first real interaction with Sauron in the finale is as the deliverer of bad news, informing his Dark Lord that half their army has deserted following Pallando's death and (presumably) the breaking of the spell he had cast upon them. And, as you can imagine, this doesn't exactly go well for him as Sauron grabs him by the throat and demands to know why he couldn't stop them.

But perhaps their last scene together holds some clues. While preparing for battle with the combined force of Númenor and the Elves, Sauron slips off his One Ring and gives himself up to his enemies. It's unlikely he'd keep carrying that on his person, so did he perhaps entrust his most "precious" creation to Theo? Is this all part of an evil plan that will see the Southlander ascend to the ultimate position of authority among the Ringwraiths? We'll sadly have to wait for Season 4.

articles.title: Blade Runner 2099 not just about AI, say star Hunter Schafer and series creator
articles.summary: Hunter Schafer and co-stars say the sci-fi TV show explores more than the idea of robotic consciousness.
body: "What does it mean to be human?" is a question that's always been at the heart of Blade Runner.
The first film in the series, released in 1982, depicted a technologically advanced yet dystopian version of Los Angeles in the then-distant future of 2019.
While the movie's flying cars haven't - quite - materialised yet in the real world, Blade Runner's themes of technological progress and the threats it poses feel just as relevant.
At least that's what the cast and crew of Blade Runner 2099, a new TV series set in the same universe, are hoping.

articles.title: Why Blade Runner 2099 Skipped Over The Replicant Uprising [Exclusive]
articles.summary: While Blade Runner 2049 set the stage for the Replicant uprising, Blade Runner 2099 skips over depicting it. Here's why showrunner Silka Luisa went this route.
body: "Welcome to a future we no longer control." So says the official tagline for the Prime Video series "Blade Runner 2099," which is set (self-evidently) 50 years after the events of Denis Villeneuve's "Blade Runner 2049" movie. The world has undergone some seriously seismic changes since then, as viewers will quickly realize in the opening moments of the show. Where both Ridley Scott's classic 1982 film "Blade Runner" and Villeneuve's 2017 sequel took place under very traditional confines (with humanity ruling over bioengineered Replicants as second-class citizens), "2099" has flipped the script entirely. Instead, the Replicants have orchestrated a full-scale uprising and seized control.

"To be honest, I feel like I've seen that before. Not with Replicants, but definitely the robot revolution is definitely something I can close my eyes and picture. It's been in the zeitgeist and people have done different takes on it, so it didn't seem like I was going to be putting anything out into the world that people couldn't imagine for themselves."
